judgment.notes: Euclidean real m-tuples and their L² norm are fixed for every natural m; the empty-coordinate space at m=0 is a singleton. No dimension bound is assumed by this definition.
Extended diameter is the supremum of pairwise extended distances in ℝ≥0∞, including the zero empty supremum; no boundedness or attainment is presumed.

Real diameter is restricted to bounded metric subsets and has empty value zero. Its identification with extended diameter is the bounded-diameter compatibility exported by N001, not an extra hypothesis on E.

The exact nested cover infima, countable index ℕ, extended scales, real exponent and nonempty-member cost agree with the frozen header. Empty costs and unsuccessful cover conditions have the correct lattice values.
Positive a and δ are explicit construction domains. C is defined by content; compatibility with real diameters is an internal N001 obligation, rather than a property granted by naming C.
H is the unnormalized gauge r↦r^a Hausdorff measure on the Borel structure, matching the pinned mkMetric definition and cover formula. No dimensional or radius prefactor is hidden.

The supremum over nonnegative exponents with infinite Hausdorff measure agrees with pinned dimH, uses the Borel structure and gives empty-set value zero. Real representatives require the separately exported finiteness in N004.
The fixed interval is exactly the real closed interval [0,1], preserving endpoints and length.
The maximum product metric is explicit on W×ℝ, with the original metric on W. Equality with Euclidean dimension is not assumed; E001 and N007 supply separate metric bridges.
L2Prod is the WithLp 2 normed product of Euclidean Rn(m) and ℝ. The squared-norm identity and coordinate identification remain M014/N007 obligations.

euclideanLift is the total underlying-pair map WithLp.toLp 2, with the correct maximum-metric domain and L²-product codomain, exactly as in the basis header. No dimension invariance is granted by its definition.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
